assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin therapy: a clear physiological discovery (gut hormone amplifying glucose-dependent insulin secretion, central effects on appetite) translated into drugs with large effects on diabetes, obesity and, increasingly, cardiovascular outcomes. Importance, clarity and impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and processing of the native peptide), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, therapeutic rationale) and Mojsov (identification of the active truncated GLP-1 form) form a plausible trio. Habener and others contributed to proglucagon/GLP-1 work and are not in the credited names, and Knudsen's drug-development role is real but more industrial; I rely on my own recollection of the history, not independent verification.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of mechanistic work and large randomized outcome trials; clinical impact is established and the field is recognized by major prizes. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Priority dispute over Mojsov versus other early GLP-1 contributors.
Whether the prize should recognize physiology or drug development; the Habener contribution is outside the credited set.
Long-term safety and durability of treatment effects are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics: a transformative method for causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity, widely adopted across neuroscience and enabling circuit dissection, including in motor systems. Originality (channelrhodopsins as genetically encoded actuators) and breadth of impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: The channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Bamberg, Hegemann) and the demonstration in neurons (Boyden and Deisseroth; Miesenboeck's earlier approach) make credit contested among six names. A three-person prize cannot capture all; I favor the molecular discovery of channelrhodopsin plus the neuronal application, but allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed in thousands of labs; clinical translation (vision restoration) is early, but as a research tool the impact is already established.
uncertainties: Whether this is a method/tool for the Prize category versus a discovery; allocation among six candidates is genuinely contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T-cell therapy: a new treatment modality producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, with strong conceptual originality and clear patient benefit.
assessment.attribution: June (CD19 CAR-T clinical translation, costimulatory domains) and Sadelain (CD28 costimulation, early design) are central; Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy and TIL work is foundational. Eshhar and others whose early chimeric receptor work is not in the credited list complicate fairness.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and years of follow-up; independent confirmation is strong. Toxicity and solid-tumor limits remain, but recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Foundational contribution of chimeric receptor pioneers outside the credited names.
Limited efficacy in solid tumors and manufacturing/toxicity issues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR as the central regulator of cell growth and nutrient responses: a fundamental conceptual advance linking nutrients, growth factors and anabolic metabolism, with relevance to cancer, immunosuppression, diabetes and ageing.
assessment.attribution: Hall's identification of TOR in yeast and demonstration of its role in growth control is the central discovery; Sabatini defined mTOR complexes and nutrient sensing. Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin was important in the chemistry. Others (Heitman, Movva, Sabers/Brown, Rall) also contributed; I am unsure about full priority and about any extraneous issues concerning a candidate's conduct.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with highly reproducible conserved pathway and approved rapalogs. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Attribution is dispersed across yeast genetics, mammalian target identification and chemistry.
Any non-scientific concerns regarding a credited individual are unverified by me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition: the paradigm of rationally targeted cancer therapy, converting CML from fatal to a chronic manageable disease. Impact and clarity are outstanding.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical translation and championing), Lydon (medicinal chemistry program, kinase inhibitor development) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms, second-generation inhibitors) form a coherent set. Upstream discoveries of BCR-ABL (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore) lie outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with over two decades of outcome data. It has already received major prizes, so the question is mostly whether the Prize wants a translational-oncology award.
uncertainties: Competition with foundational BCR-ABL discoveries not credited here.
Medicine Nobel prefers discoveries over drug development in some eras.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 as a regulator of survival rather than proliferation, opening the genetic control of apoptosis in cancer and leading to venetoclax. A conceptual advance with a clear translational endpoint.
assessment.attribution: Adams and Cory (BCL-2 family biology) and Vaux (BCL-2 as a cell death inhibitor, cooperation with MYC) are strong; Strasser's and Korsmeyer's/Tsujimoto's contributions complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with clinical validation via BH3 mimetics. Apoptosis was recognized in 2002 (Brenner, Horvitz, Sulston), which lessens novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize area and with Tsujimoto/Korsmeyer, who are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation as a cellular substrate of memory: a foundational and widely tested synaptic-plasticity phenomenon, clear in definition and originality (Bliss and Lømo 1973) with NMDA-receptor mechanisms (Collingridge).
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo made the original discovery; Collingridge established NMDA-receptor dependence. Morris's behavioral work links LTP to learning but would fall outside a three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, though the causal link between LTP and memory has remained partly debated, and downstream translational impact is limited.
uncertainties: Strength of the causal LTP-memory link remains debated.
Four credited names exceed the three-laureate limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen): mechanistic RNA biology producing an effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, a disease with dramatic clinical change in infants. Strong clarity and clinical importance, and relevant to motor neuron disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO design for SMN2) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are well matched. Other contributors (Hua, Singh, Adrian's collaborators, the clinical team) could be included.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with real-world follow-up; confirmation is strong. Antisense modalities have recently been recognized in other areas, so timing is plausible but not urgent.
uncertainties: Credit among chemistry, splicing and clinical development contributors is not fully settled.
Novel gene-therapy competitors for SMA complicate the narrative.
